drug_identity.active_ingredient: Medium chain triglycerides (principally C8 and C10 saturated fatty acids)
drug_identity.off_label_note: All usages listed for dogs are extra-label.

metabolism_and_clearance.extra_information: More readily hydrolyzed than conventional food fat. Can pass through intestinal membranes into venous blood circulation without bile acids or pancreatic lipase. Hepatically converted into ketone bodies.

organ_burden_logic.note: Based on pharmacokinetics and reported adverse effects.

brain.evidence: May play a supporting role in prevention or treating cognitive dysfunction syndromes. Decreased seizure frequency in idiopathic epilepsy.

liver.evidence: Use with caution in patients with significant hepatic disease; impaired hepatic clearance can lead to high systemic levels of medium chain fatty acids, precipitating or exacerbating hepatic coma.

brain.evidence: May play a supporting role in prevention or treating cognitive dysfunction syndromes.

liver.evidence: Higher dosages of MCT oil may induce hepatic lipidosis in cats.

timing_profile.evidence: Rapidly absorbed via the portal vein.

_ddi_note: Could theoretically affect absorption of drugs that are dependent on fat for oral absorption (e.g., griseofulvin, fat-soluble vitamins).

drug_interactions.drug: Fat-dependent absorption drugs (e.g., griseofulvin, fat-soluble vitamins)
drug_interactions.evidence: Could theoretically affect absorption of drugs that are dependent on fat for oral absorption.

dosage_list.context: Offset caloric reduction when dietary long chain triglycerides are restricted

hepatic_dose_adjustment.note: Use with caution in patients with significant hepatic disease (e.g., portacaval shunts, cirrhosis). In cats, higher dosages may induce hepatic lipidosis.

effects_and_mechanisms.common_mechanism: More readily hydrolyzed than conventional food fat. Can pass through intestinal membranes into venous blood circulation without bile acids or pancreatic lipase. Hepatically converted into ketone bodies used for fuel in the brain.

species_notes.dog: Many clinicians bypass MCT oil due to expense and unpalatability to dogs.
species_notes.cat: May be useful as a base-vehicle to administer drugs to cats; owner-perceived acceptability was significantly higher than gelatin capsules.

dog.evidence: Use with caution in animals with significant hepatic disease. Avoid during DKA.

cat.evidence: Use with caution in animals with significant hepatic disease. Avoid during DKA. Higher dosages may induce hepatic lipidosis.

storage_and_forms.storage: Store at room temperature in glass bottles, protected from light.

section_1_2_10.highlights: Lipid sometimes used to provide calories and fatty acids to dogs with restricted fat intake; may have benefit in canine epilepsy. Most clinicians use dietary therapy instead. Use with caution in animals with significant hepatic disease. Adverse effects include unpalatability, bloating, flatulence, and diarrhea; may induce hepatic lipidosis in cats.
section_1_2_10.indications: Offset caloric reduction when dietary long chain triglycerides are restricted (e.g., chronic infiltrative diseases of small intestine, fat malabsorption). Adjunct for canine idiopathic epilepsy. Useful as a base-vehicle to administer drugs to cats. May play a supporting role in cognitive dysfunction syndromes.
section_1_2_10.client_info: Because of the unpalatability of the oil, it should be mixed with small quantities of food before offering to the animal. Contact your veterinarian if you notice side effects, including diarrhea or flatulence.
